### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Medium-High — international SPSP authorship; cross-cultural quantitative work regularly published (1,431 articles on "Cultural Differences and Values" per OpenAlex) |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Low-Medium — non-Western data accepted within mainstream personality/social psychology framework |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — diversity, race, gender, sexual identity papers regularly published |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Mainstream personality/social psychology — social/intergroup (2,613 articles), cultural differences (1,431), behavioral health (908), moral/emotional judgment (788), evolutionary psychology (584), attachment (534) per OpenAlex |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must engage **mainstream personality / social psychology** with empirical evidence. SAGE Track submission system. COPE member; confidential ethical peer review.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Authors asked NOT to share decision letters or reviews publicly (confidentiality norm). Split decisions (one reject, one accept-with-minor) can lead to rejection (community evidence: scirev.org reviewer anecdote 2026-05).

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from the personality and social psychology research community — SPSP (Society for Personality and Social Psychology) faculty and senior researchers. SAGE Track submission system. COPE member with confidential ethical peer review. Common reviewer demands focused on multi-study programmatic packages, theoretical contribution, and quantitative rigor. Split-decision dynamics (one reject + one accept-with-minor) can lead to rejection (community evidence: scirev anecdote 2026-05).

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Personality + social psychology researchers | https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psp |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International SPSP-affiliated programs | https://scirev.org/reviews/personality-and-social-psychology-bulletin/ |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Single-study designs without strong theoretical justification
- Pure qualitative submissions
- Public discussion of decision letters or reviews (confidentiality norm; community evidence: journals.sagepub.com 2026-05)
- Failure to disclose AI use per SAGE publisher policy
- Manuscripts outside personality/social psychology scope

### Soft Tax

Low for SPSP-aligned multi-study quantitative authors. Free OA option likely via SAGE Choice (no fees to submit or publish under subscription model per community evidence 2026-05).

### Best Suited For

- Multi-study quantitative personality / social psychology programs (peer of JPSP at slightly lower acceptance bar)
- Social identity, cultural differences, moral judgment empirical work
- Attachment, relationship-dynamics, social-influence research
- Terror management theory empirical work
- Meta-analyses of personality/social-psychology literatures
- SPSP-community-targeted research

### Not Recommended For

- Pure autoethnography or first-person work
- Single-case qualitative analyses
- Critical / discursive psychology (consider Theory & Psychology)
- Cultural-psychology dialogical-self work (consider Culture & Psychology)
- Authors needing public reviewer-experience discussion

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Self and Identity](./self-and-identity.md) | Identity-focused empirical psychology; T&F-published; comparable quantitative paradigm |
| 2 | [Personality and Individual Differences](./personality-and-individual-differences.md) | If individual-differences focused; ISSID; broader methodological tolerance |
| 3 | [Journal of Personality and Social Psychology](./journal-of-personality-and-social-psychology.md) | Higher-tier same family if work can be developed into full multi-study program |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JPSP as "good but not flagship-level," PSPB is often a better fit because: SPSP-affiliated identical community; comparable empirical-multistudy paradigm; slightly lower acceptance bar; monthly publication accommodates faster turnaround.
